statusLegend.listed: The provider's own page lists this country as supported.
statusLegend.not-excluded: The country is not on the provider's published list of unsupported countries.
statusLegend.invite-only: The provider says new accounts from this country are invite-only.
statusLegend.label-only: The provider lists the country with a label it does not explain on that page. Ask the provider what it means for you.
statusLegend.conditional: Supported only under conditions described in the note.
statusLegend.grandfathered-only: Only existing merchants are kept. New merchants from this country are not eligible.
statusLegend.not-listed: The country does not appear on the provider's supported list.
statusLegend.prohibited: The provider names this country on its prohibited list.
statusLegend.unknown: We could not verify this on the provider's own site.

providers.name: Polar
providers.summary: Merchant of record aimed at developers. Payouts go through Stripe Connect Express, and Polar publishes its own payout country list.

facts.label: Seller countries
facts.value: Countries where Polar can pay out through Stripe Connect Express, per Polar's list. Polar's FAQ says this works in places where Stripe itself is invite-only, such as India.

facts.label: Fees
facts.value: Starter (free): 5% + 50 cents. Pro ($20/month): 3.8% + 40 cents. Growth ($100/month): 3.6% + 35 cents. Scale ($400/month): 3.4% + 30 cents. Plus 1.5% for international (non-US) cards.

facts.label: Payout fees
facts.value: Stripe payout fees passed through: $2 per month with active payouts, 0.25% + 25 cents per payout, and cross-border FX from 0.25% (EU) to 1% elsewhere.

facts.label: Early Member rate
facts.value: Organizations created before May 27, 2026: 4% + 40 cents, plus 0.5% on subscriptions.

facts.label: Subscription fee
facts.value: No separate subscription fee on Starter or paid plans.

facts.label: Product rules
facts.value: Accepts software and SaaS, digital products, and premium content and access. Prohibits physical goods, human services and marketplaces, among others. Directories, eBooks, AI content generation, marketing tools and VPNs get closer review. Policy effective October 1, 2026.

providers.name: Dodo Payments
providers.summary: Merchant of record. Eligibility is based on the country of your government ID, and for companies, on every director and beneficial owner too.

facts.label: Eligibility rule
facts.value: Individuals: country of government ID. Entities: incorporation country plus the ID country of every director and beneficial owner. Dodo says registering a company in a supported country does not by itself make you eligible.

facts.label: Grandfathered countries
facts.value: Since March 23, 2026, merchants from Bangladesh, Egypt, Equatorial Guinea, Eritrea, Marshall Islands, Micronesia, Morocco, Nauru, Nigeria, Tuvalu and Ukraine who joined before the change are kept. New merchants from these countries are not eligible.

facts.label: Fees
facts.value: 4% + 40 cents for US domestic cards, plus 1.5% for international cards and 0.5% for subscriptions. India domestic INR payments: 4% + 15 cents. PayPal and BNPL add 3%.

facts.label: Other fees
facts.value: Disputes $30. Refunds $1. USD SWIFT payouts $25.

facts.label: Payout fees
facts.value: Standard payouts free, with a $5 fee if the payout is under $1,000. Standard FX on non-USD settlements. USD SWIFT payouts $25.

facts.label: Bank debits
facts.value: ACH and SEPA: 1.5%, capped at $15 or 15 euros.

facts.label: Product rules
facts.value: Welcomes SaaS and AI products, digital goods, and templates, plugins and apps. Lists 32 prohibited categories, including manual digital services, physical goods, gaming and virtual goods, hosting and VPNs, and marketplaces. AI content generation, marketing tools, e-books and productised services get extra review.
